subject: Embedding integration: dimensions, batching, and migration plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme-retail.com>, Leila Gomez <leila@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Embedding integration: dimensions, batching, and migration plan

Hi Samir / Leila — thanks for the call today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared checklist.

Summary of what we heard from your side:
- Goal: Replace Vectorly embeddings for product search and recommendations, keep existing search UX but reduce latency and cost.
- Current corpus: ~3.2M product vectors, ~2 updates/day, peak QPS ~150, steady QPS ~40.
- Desired SLO: <150ms p95 for nearest-neighbour retrieval in US-WEST region; reranker latency budget ~120ms.
- Reranker: hybrid approach — candidate set ~100, then a semantic rerank (ML model) on top.

Architecture / integration items we discussed and items for Redwood input: 
1) Vector dimension and normalization: you mentioned Vectorly uses 1536 dims today. Confirm if you want to preserve 1536 or down-project to 1024 for cost? If you keep 1536 we recommend pre-normalizing (L2) on write for fast dot-product/cosine at query time.
2) Batch ingestion: goal is a one-time migration of ~3.2M vectors. For the POC we'll do a 200k subset. We recommend batched ingest workers that emit 1k-4k vectors per job depending on memory. Please confirm preferred chunk size and whether you want us to run the worker in your VPC or via Redwood-managed pipeline.
3) Auth & SDK: we support API-key, short-lived JWTs for server-to-server, and workload identity for cloud VMs. For ingestion jobs we usually use a short-lived JWT + rotated key. Which option suits procurement?
4) Routing / zones: primary routing to us-west; fallback to eu-west if us-west capacity is constrained. Confirm regulatory constraints for EU data residency.
5) Reranker integration: we support structured output / tool-calling where the reranker can call the Redwood embeddings endpoint for candidate expansion and then call your reranker service. We need interface details for the reranker model (input format, batch size).

Proposed next steps (short):
- Ben: supply SDK ingestion pattern + recommended normalization strategy (action: Ben) — by Mon 12/21
- Marissa: send mutual action plan + SOC2 + PO checklist (action: Marissa) — by Tue 12/22
- Samir: confirm desired final embedding dim (1536 vs 1024) and whether you want Redwood-managed ingestion or in-VPC worker (action: Acme) — by Tue 12/22
- Schedule 30m POC kickoff to align on runbook and credentials (I'll send a link)

Attachments: I attached an initial spec template (acme_embed_spec_v1.pdf) and our ingest runbook stub.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@acme-retail.com>, Leila Gomez <leila@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embedding integration: dimensions, batching, and migration plan

Jordan — adding technical clarifications based on what I sketched in the call. TL;DR: preserve 1536 unless cost target forces 1024; pre-normalize on write; batch ingestion worker with checkpointing.

Details: 
- Dimension: 1536 is fine. If you later want to reduce space/cost we can run a PCA down-projection offline; for now preserve 1536 to avoid model drift.
- Normalization: two options:
  * Pre-normalize (recommended): store L2-normalized vectors at write time. This allows nearest-neighbor via dot-product with normalized queries (fast, stable).
  * Store raw + normalize at query time: more flexible for different similarity metrics, but increases query-time cost.
- Ingest batching: for the POC use chunk size = 2,000 vectors per job. For full migration we recommend 1k–4k per worker depending on memory; we'll run a controlled test to pick the sweet spot. We'll use parallel workers (N=8–16) to hit throughput targets without overloading your database/network.
- Quantization: 8-bit (int8/LLM-friendly) is ok for cold storage, but for top-k reranking we recommend FP16 on the retrieval nodes to avoid rank inversion for close neighbors.
- Reranker flow: typical pattern: retrieve top 100 candidates via approximate nearest neighbor on normalized embeddings, then call reranker model in batches of 8–16 inputs (per GPU). The reranker should get the original text + contextual features. Redwood can stream the reranker candidates back via structured JSON with scores (we support tool-calling payloads like {"candidates": [...], "scores": [...]}) so your reranker can be a separate service if you prefer.

Quick SDK snippets (pseudo):
- Ingest (python):
  from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
  client = EmbeddingsClient(api_key=...)
  client.ingest_batch(vectors=batch_vectors, ids=batch_ids, normalize=True)

- Query (curl):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \n    -d '{"vector": [...], "top_k":100}' \n    https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings/lookup

Notes on auth: we can issue short-lived JWTs that your ingestion workers can use; if you want Redwood-managed ingestion we just need a service account key + destination index name. For in-VPC workers we'll provide a helm chart / docker image.

I'll attach the ingest runbook (ingest_runbook_v0.3.md) with exact memory estimates and backoff logic.

Ben Carter
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Embedding integration: dimensions, batching, and migration plan

Hi Samir / Leila — following up with a short mutual action plan and ask list so procurement and your platform team have what they need.

Mutual action plan (high level):
- 12/23: POC kickoff call (30m) — agree on POC index name, credentials, and test dataset (we'll use a 200k subset).
- 12/24–01/05: POC ingest + validation (Redwood runs ingest if you want us to; otherwise we'll provide the worker image).
- 01/06–01/12: performance tuning (batch sizing, quantization, reranker latency tuning).
- 01/15: go/no-go review and pricing estimate for full migration.

What we need from Acme to start the POC:
- Confirmation of embedding dimension (1536) — yes/no (Samir)
- A service account or allowlist IPs for ingestion workers (for in-VPC option)
- Any data residency constraints for EU — you mentioned none for product catalog but confirm in writing
- PO or procurement kickoff timeline (procurement contact + template)

Files attached: ingest_runbook_v0.3.md (contains backoff/backpressure recipe, chunking guidance, retry semantics) and acme_embed_spec_v1.pdf (fields we expect: id, title, category, price, free-text description, locale).

I'll draft the PO checklist and SOC2 evidence pack and send those by EOD.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Embedding integration: dimensions, batching, and migration plan

Jordan / team — thanks for the clear notes. Confirming a few items inline: 
- Dimension: we will preserve 1536 for POC (will re-evaluate after perf/cost numbers).
- Ingestion: Acme prefers Redwood to run the POC-managed ingestion (faster kickoff). We'll provide a service account and a VPN tunnel for the ingest worker.
- Regional constraints: Catalog data stays in US; no EU residency required.

Two asks from my side: 
1) Can you provide a ballpark cost estimate for 1M retrieval queries per month (including reranker compute) so I can feed procurement?
2) Can you confirm the expected time to complete the 200k vectors POC ingest (end-to-end) if Redwood runs it?

Also — appreciate the attachments. Please include the SOC2 summary and the runbook link in the kickoff invite.

Thanks — Samir
